samples.summary: A third, independently-defined blockquote-prefix regex — no shared helper for "what is a quote prefix" in the notes view
samples.evidence: This change adds `QUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/` in list-commands.ts:45 and, in the same PR, an inline `( {0,3}(?:> ?)*\s*)` prefix group in checkbox-input.ts:9, while `packages/notes/src/view/commands.ts:278` already owns `const QUOTE_RE = /^\s*>\s?/` for `toggleQuote`. Three definitions of the same syntactic concept now coexist and already disagree: commands.ts accepts any amount of leading whitespace before the `>` and consumes any single whitespace after it, whereas the new ones cap the pre-quote indent at three spaces and only accept a literal space. So a line like `    > - a` is 'quoted' to the quote toggle but 'unquoted, indented' to the list commands and the checkbox input — the toolbar's own notion of block containment is not consistent across buttons, and a future fix to one regex will not reach the other two. Peeling the quote prefix off a line is exactly the kind of parsing the repo would put in one place (a shared `quotePrefixOf(text)` in the notes view module) and reuse from all three call sites.

samples.summary: Unrelated accessibility feature (task-checkbox `aria-label`) bundled into the blockquote-list change
samples.evidence: Every other hunk of this change is about one behaviour: making list commands, the bare-checkbox input handler and `setTaskChecked` operate *inside* a blockquote prefix. The `taskItemText()` helper (preview.ts:185-200) and the new `aria-label` write in `render()` are a separate accessible-name concern with its own test ('names each checkbox after its own item text') and its own design-doc paragraph (docs/design/notes/notes.md:808-812). It is plausibly desirable, but it is not derivable from the blockquote outcome, so it lands as unrequested scope in this PR: the two behaviours can no longer be reverted or bisected independently. No originating issue text accompanies the change, so I cannot confirm both were asked for.

samples.summary: Incidental reformat of an untouched mermaid test
samples.evidence: The last hunk rewraps the `preview.render(...)` call in the mermaid cache test purely as formatting; it has nothing to do with blockquotes or checkbox labels and adds diff noise to a file otherwise changed for substantive reasons.
